accepted.s: Which one of the following was the first tiger reserve under Project Tiger?
accepted.x: Corbett was the first tiger reserve under Project Tiger, formally included on 1 April 1973.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first reserve from other reserves associated with the programme.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Project Tiger commenced with how many reserves covering approximately what area?
accepted.x: Project Tiger began with nine reserves covering 18,278 square kilometres.
accepted.tq: Match the programme’s starting figures as a combined number-and-area fact.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Project Tiger is/are correct?
1. It was launched on the advice of a task force set up by Indira Gandhi.
2. WWF support was associated with its launch.
3. Palamau was among the first nine tiger reserves.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Project Tiger was launched on the advice of Indira Gandhi’s task force, had WWF support, and included Palamau among its first nine reserves.
accepted.tq: Check each historical association separately before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) is a:
o: statutory body created by the 2006 amendment to the Wildlife Protection Act
constitutional body created by the 42nd Amendment
judicial body established under the Forest Rights Act
accepted.x: The NTCA is a statutory body created through the 2006 amendment to the Wildlife Protection Act.
accepted.tq: Use the statutory-versus-constitutional distinction and identify the enabling law.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who chairs the National Tiger Conservation Authority?
o: The Chief Minister of the concerned State
accepted.x: The NTCA is chaired by the Union Environment Minister.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who holds this authority?’ method to distinguish the responsible office.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Section 38V(3) of the Wildlife Protection Act, each State is required to prepare a:
o: Wildlife Census Plan for every national park
Tiger Conservation Plan for every tiger reserve
National Biodiversity Register for every forest division
Species Recovery Plan for every district
accepted.x: Section 38V(3) requires each State to prepare a Tiger Conservation Plan for every tiger reserve.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact statutory provision by matching the section with its prescribed document.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the All India Tiger Estimation:
1. It is conducted every four years.
2. Camera traps are used in the estimation process.
3. The M-STrIPES monitoring system is used.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The All India Tiger Estimation is conducted every four years and uses both camera traps and the M-STrIPES monitoring system.
accepted.tq: Test a set of closely related methodological features together.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The number of tigers estimated in India in 2006 was:
accepted.x: The 2006 tiger estimate recorded 1,411 tigers.
accepted.tq: Use the direct numerical-recall pattern for a census benchmark.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The annual growth rate associated with the 2022 tiger estimate was approximately:
accepted.x: The 2022 estimate was associated with an annual growth rate of 6.1%.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the growth-rate figure from the population totals.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India holds approximately what share of the world’s wild tiger population?
accepted.x: India holds approximately 70–75% of the world’s wild tigers.
accepted.tq: Use the range rather than confusing it with an exact census figure.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The TX2 goal adopted at the Global Tiger Summit was to:
o: double the population of wild tigers by 2022
create two tiger reserves in every State by 2022
increase India’s tiger population twofold by 2010
accepted.x: TX2 was the goal of doubling the global population of wild tigers by 2022.
accepted.tq: Decode the named international target by linking the abbreviation with its stated objective.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Global Tiger Summit of 2010?
1. It was held in St Petersburg in November 2010.
2. It set the TX2 goal.
3. International Tiger Day on 29 July traces its origin to this effort.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The summit was held in St Petersburg in November 2010, adopted TX2, and is associated with International Tiger Day on 29 July.
accepted.tq: Combine event location, date, objective and legacy in a coded statement question.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India’s achievement in relation to the TX2 target is best described as:
o: India reached the target only after 2025.
India was excluded from the target.
India reached the target ahead of schedule.
accepted.x: India achieved the TX2 target ahead of schedule.
accepted.tq: Test the trend or outcome of a named international conservation target.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Institution or initiative)
 a. Global Tiger Forum
 b. IBCA
 c. ITHCP
 d. CA|TS

List-II (Associated description)
 i. Led by IUCN
 ii. Headquarters at New Delhi
 iii. Global effort for tiger conservation
 iv. Global effort for tiger conservation

Codes:
 a  b  c  d
1. ii  iii  i  iv
2. iii  ii  iv  i
3. ii  iv  i  iii
4. iv  ii  iii  i
accepted.x: The Global Tiger Forum has its headquarters at New Delhi; IBCA and CA|TS are other global efforts, while ITHCP is led by IUCN. The matching is a–ii, b–iv, c–i, d–iii.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair linking the Global Tiger Forum with its headquarters.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Andhra Pradesh tiger-conservation initiative?
o: NSTR — headquarters of the Global Tiger Forum
Seshachalam — venue of the 2010 Global Tiger Summit
NSTR — India’s largest tiger reserve by core area
Seshachalam — first reserve under Project Tiger
accepted.x: NSTR is described as India’s largest tiger reserve by core area and lies in the Nallamala hills.
accepted.tq: Use the location-and-status distinction to identify the correct regional association.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The approximate core area attributed to NSTR in the Nallamala hills is:
accepted.x: NSTR has an approximate core area of 5,443 square kilometres in the Nallamala hills.
accepted.tq: Recall the reserve-specific area figure rather than the national Project Tiger area.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh tiger-conservation plan described, four female tigers are to be moved into NSTR from:
accepted.x: Four female tigers are to be moved into NSTR, two each from Chandrapur in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Test the source locations and the two-each distribution together.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The number of anti-poaching camps in the NSTR initiative is proposed to be increased from 89 to:
accepted.x: The number of anti-poaching camps is proposed to rise from 89 to 150.
accepted.tq: Recall the before-and-after numerical pair in a conservation-management measure.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the NSTR–Seshachalam landscape is/are correct?
1. It has 68 tigers and 11 cubs.
2. Gaurs are being reintroduced in the landscape.
3. Four female tigers are to be moved into the landscape, two each from Chandrapur and Madhya Pradesh.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The landscape has 68 tigers and 11 cubs; gaurs are being reintroduced; and four female tigers are planned for translocation from Chandrapur and Madhya Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Verify several regional conservation actions without confusing population counts with translocation figures.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Projects located in tiger corridors require clearance from the:
o: Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife
accepted.x: Projects in tiger corridors require clearance from the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the competent wildlife authority.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The third railway line mentioned as a threat is associated with which tiger corridor?
accepted.x: A third railway line threatens the Satpura–Melghat tiger corridor.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a specific threatened corridor and other conservation landscapes.
accepted.sec: Project Tiger - launch, first reserve, NTCA, census, trend, summit, AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Convention on Migratory Species (CMS):
1. It is also known as the Bonn Convention.
2. It was signed in 1979.
3. It functions under UNEP.
4. India is a party to it.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: CMS is the Bonn Convention, was signed in 1979, operates under UNEP, and India is a party to it.
accepted.tq: Check the treaty’s alternate name, date, institutional location and membership together.
accepted.sec: Migratory species - CMS COP13 listings, Amur falcon  [APPSC]

accepted.s: CMS COP13 was held at:
accepted.x: The 13th Conference of the Parties to CMS was held in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, in February 2020.
accepted.tq: Separate the closely related CMS COP13 and COP14 locations and years.
accepted.sec: Migratory species - CMS COP13 listings, Amur falcon  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the mascot of CMS COP13?
o: Gibi, representing the Great Indian Bustard
accepted.x: The mascot of CMS COP13 was ‘Gibi’, representing the Great Indian Bustard.
accepted.tq: Test the event mascot against nearby species-related conservation names.
accepted.sec: Migratory species - CMS COP13 listings, Amur falcon  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
At CMS COP13, which of the following species were added to Appendix I?
1. Great Indian Bustard
2. Asian elephant
3. Bengal florican

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Great Indian Bustard, Asian elephant and Bengal florican were added to Appendix I at CMS COP13.
accepted.tq: Test the complete species list by checking whether any item has been omitted.
accepted.sec: Migratory species - CMS COP13 listings, Amur falcon  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the migration route of the Amur falcon?
o: It breeds in India and migrates to Central Asia through Europe.
It breeds in Southeast Russia and northern China and migrates to southern Africa.
It breeds in Australia and migrates to the Arabian Peninsula.
It breeds in southern Africa and migrates to northern China.
accepted.x: The Amur falcon breeds in Southeast Russia and northern China and migrates to southern Africa.
accepted.tq: Trace the species’ breeding and wintering regions in the correct direction.
accepted.sec: Migratory species - CMS COP13 listings, Amur falcon  [APPSC]

accepted.s: During its migration, the Amur falcon is associated with which place in Nagaland?
accepted.x: The Amur falcon stops in huge numbers at Doyang reservoir near Pangti in Nagaland, known as the ‘Falcon Capital of the World’.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive place-name association to identify the correct migratory stopover.
accepted.sec: Migratory species - CMS COP13 listings, Amur falcon  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which statement regarding the Amur falcon is correct?
1. Its migration includes a non-stop crossing of the Arabian Sea.
2. It is regarded as one of the longest raptor migrations.
3. Pangti is known as the ‘Falcon Capital of the World’.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Amur falcon undertakes a very long raptor migration, crosses the Arabian Sea non-stop and is strongly associated with Pangti.
accepted.tq: Combine route, migration significance and local place-name facts in one coded question.
accepted.sec: Migratory species - CMS COP13 listings, Amur falcon  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal cause of the decline of vultures in India was the consumption of cattle carcasses containing:
accepted.x: Vultures declined sharply after feeding on cattle carcasses containing veterinary diclofenac.
accepted.tq: Use the cause-and-effect pattern linking a veterinary drug with wildlife decline.
accepted.sec: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: Diclofenac causes death in vultures primarily by leading to:
accepted.x: Diclofenac causes kidney failure in vultures, resulting in visceral gout.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the biological mechanism from the broader population-level consequence.
accepted.sec: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: Veterinary diclofenac was banned in India in:
accepted.x: Veterinary diclofenac was banned in May 2006. The decline had been noticed at Keoladeo in 1998.
accepted.tq: Separate the year of decline observation from the year of the drug ban.
accepted.sec: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following veterinary drugs were banned for animal use in 2023?
1. Aceclofenac
2. Ketoprofen
3. Diclofenac

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Aceclofenac and ketoprofen were banned for animal use in 2023. Diclofenac had already been banned in 2006.
accepted.tq: Use the date distinction to separate the 2023 bans from the earlier diclofenac ban.
accepted.sec: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is regarded as a safe alternative to veterinary diclofenac for livestock treatment?
accepted.x: Meloxicam is identified as a safe alternative to diclofenac in the context of vulture conservation.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the recommended alternative from drugs associated with vulture mortality or bans.
accepted.sec: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres  [other exams]

accepted.s:
The Action Plan for Vulture Conservation 2020–25 called for: 
1. A State-level vulture committee in every State.
2. Establishment of more vulture breeding centres.
3. Extension of the plan up to 2030.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The 2020–25 Action Plan called for State-level committees and more breeding centres. Its extension up to 2030 is a subsequent development, not part of the original call described here.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that belongs to a later development rather than the original action plan.
accepted.sec: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Action Plan for Vulture Conservation 2020–25 was subsequently:
accepted.x: The Action Plan for Vulture Conservation 2020–25 was extended to 2030.
accepted.tq: Test the temporal continuation of a named conservation plan.
accepted.sec: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: The first vulture conservation breeding centre in India was established at:
accepted.x: The Jatayu Conservation Breeding Centre at Pinjore in Haryana was the first vulture conservation breeding centre.
accepted.tq: Match the first facility with its location and avoid confusing it with a vulture-safe landscape.
accepted.sec: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which organisation is the partner consortium associated with vulture conservation breeding efforts?
accepted.x: SAVE, meaning Saving Asia’s Vultures from Extinction, is the partner consortium associated with these efforts.
accepted.tq: Expand the acronym and distinguish the vulture consortium from tiger and migratory-species institutions.
accepted.sec: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: The first attempt to release a captive-bred vulture in the Nilgiris landscape in 2026:
o: was cancelled before any bird was released
was fully successful and produced a breeding colony
failed because the bird did not settle and subsequently died
resulted in the bird being transferred to Pinjore
accepted.x: The first 2026 release attempt in the Nilgiris failed because the bird did not settle and died.
accepted.tq: Test the outcome of a conservation intervention rather than assuming that release means success.
accepted.sec: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: Vultures are included under which conservation framework?
accepted.x: Vultures are included in the Species Recovery Programme.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the species-recovery framework from tiger-specific monitoring and targets.
accepted.sec: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: India has how many recognised vulture species, of which how many are critically endangered?
accepted.x: India has nine vulture species, of which four are critically endangered.
accepted.tq: Recall the paired total-and-subset figures in a biodiversity question.
accepted.sec: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following groups consists entirely of the four critically endangered vulture species identified in India?
1. White-rumped vulture
2. Slender-billed vulture
3. Long-billed vulture
4. Red-headed vulture

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The four critically endangered species listed are the white-rumped, slender-billed, long-billed and red-headed vultures.
accepted.tq: Check whether the complete named list has been reproduced without omission.
accepted.sec: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: The decline of vultures was first noticed at Keoladeo in:
accepted.x: The decline in the vulture population was noticed at Keoladeo in 1998.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the initial observation year from later policy and action-plan years.
accepted.sec: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the first vulture conservation portal?
accepted.x: ‘The Vulture Network’ is identified as the first vulture conservation portal.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact institutional name rather than a related conservation initiative.
accepted.sec: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres  [other exams]

accepted.s: Vulture Safe Zones are primarily intended to:
o: promote the use of veterinary diclofenac
provide landscapes where vultures are protected from major threats such as toxic veterinary drugs
accepted.x: Vulture Safe Zones are conservation landscapes intended to protect vultures from threats such as toxic veterinary drugs and related mortality.
accepted.tq: Apply the purpose of a conservation designation to a practical wildlife-management situation.
accepted.sec: Vultures - decline, diclofenac ban, action plan, breeding centres  [other exams]
